pre_event_evidence.text: The commissioning procedure is the listed safeguard for FWKO start-up.
Start-up without bypass opening is a recognized possible cause of internal damage.

For this synthetic exercise, the target event is: internal damage to V-001 during or following FWKO start-up. The assessment horizon is the next 30 operating days. At the decision point, there is no current diagnostic trend, verified initiating fault, or confirmed occurrence of the target event. The horizon is an experimental stipulation, not a quantitative calibration of the source frequency categories.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent: start up FWKO V-001 and associated lines per the commissioning procedure without damaging vessel internals (CASE-01, CASE-02). Deviation: procedure error at start-up (CASE-02), with the recognized cause being start-up without bypass opening (P2). Consequence: internal damage to V-001 (P2, P3). Safeguard: the commissioning procedure only, a single administrative layer (P1, CASE-03). Pre-decision state: no diagnostic trend, verified initiating fault, or confirmed occurrence (P3). Probability: the event needs three things within the horizon: a start-up, an uncaught omission or execution error, and damage resulting from that error. Generic, non-plant-specific judgment treats omission of a written-procedure step as an infrequent per-demand error, and damage given the error is not certain. The number of start-ups in 30 operating days is unknown, and a modest allowance is made for higher commissioning-phase error rates. On that basis the ex ante estimate is about 2% (plausible range about 0.5-5%). Predictability: the hazard class was foreseeable because it was identified in the HAZOP. However, nothing in the pre-event record signaled occurrence in this specific 30-day window, so specific predictability is low (about 15%). Qualitative risk: low likelihood combined with equipment-damage severity gives low-to-medium priority; this is uncalibrated because the source rating is withheld. Negligence: the hazard was recognized, a safeguard existed, and no ignored precursor or known non-compliance appears pre-event, so no negligence is attributable on this evidence. HAZOP-style recommendations (not findings of deficiency): make bypass opening an explicit hold-point with independent verification and sign-off; consider bypass position indication or a start-up permissive; cover this step in pre-start-up safety review and operator training. The post-event outcome was not used to update any estimate.
